correctness.rationale: The orthonormal-frame identity supplies a row with perpendicular energy >=1/(N-1); determinant/trace bounds give sigma_min^2 >=1/[2(N-1)]. Every E-optimal pair therefore has condition number <=sqrt(2(N-1)). The explicit axis-supported N-row frame has orthonormal columns, all E-optimal pairs with singulars (a,2t) and condition sqrt(N-3), and another pair tI with condition one. The embedded checker reproduced exhaustive pair comparisons in representative dimensions and 4,600 random-frame diagnostics; the infinite result is analytical.

value.rationale: Deterministic row-subset embedding algorithms optimize least singular value to protect approximation error; condition distortion is a separate natural objective. The new construction shows their global optima can deviate by unbounded sqrt(N), and the universal inequality proves this is the correct dimensional scale, rather than just an isolated numerical or zero-risk warning. The limitation is structural, on exactly orthonormal two-column inputs, and relevant to interpreting E-optimal row selection; it does not claim full solver-performance consequences.
